featured_media.title: The Benefits and Myths of Circumcision: What Every Parent Should Know

content:
When considering circumcision for your new born, the decision can feel daunting. With a variety of opinions, myths, and facts circulating on the internet, it's essential to get accurate, reliable information. At Circumcision in London, we aim to educate parents on this important topic so that they can make informed choices for their child. This article explores the health benefits of circumcision, dispels common myths and provides a clear understanding of what to expect when choosing this procedure.

What is Circumcision?

Circumcision is the surgical removal of the foreskin, the skin covering the head of the penis. This practice dates back thousands of years and is performed for various reasons, including religious, cultural and medical. In modern times, circumcision has become a common procedure across many countries, particularly in new born boys.

Benefits of Circumcision

  • Improved Hygiene: One of the most frequently cited reasons for circumcision is hygiene. Removing the foreskin makes it easier to clean the penis, reducing the likelihood of infections, such as urinary tract infections (UTIs). While proper hygiene can be maintained without circumcision, many parents appreciate the convenience and reduced risk of complications later in life.
  • Reduced Risk of Infections: Studies have shown that circumcision can reduce the risk of urinary tract infections, especially in infancy. UTIs can be serious if left untreated and circumcised boys have a significantly lower chance of developing these infections.
  • Decreased Risk of Certain STIs: Research has found that circumcision lowers the risk of contracting sexually transmitted infections (STIs) such as HIV, HPV and herpes. This is due to the fact that the foreskin can harbour bacteria and viruses, increasing the likelihood of transmission.
  • Lower Risk of Penile Cancer: While penile cancer is rare, circumcision has been shown to reduce the risk further. According to the American Cancer Society, circumcised men have a lower chance of developing penile cancer compared to those who are uncircumcised.
  • Fewer Complications with Phimosis: Phimosis, a condition where the foreskin is too tight to be retracted over the head of the penis, can lead to discomfort and infections. Circumcision eliminates the possibility of phimosis and its associated complications.

Common Myths About Circumcision

Despite the proven benefits, several myths surrounding circumcision continue to cause confusion. Let's take a moment to address these misconceptions:

Myth 1: Circumcision Reduces Sexual Sensitivity

One of the most persistent myths is that circumcision decreases sexual pleasure. However, numerous studies indicate that circumcised men do not experience a significant difference in sensitivity compared to those who are uncircumcised. In fact, many men report no change in sexual satisfaction after circumcision.

Myth 2: Circumcision is a Risky Procedure

Circumcision is a relatively simple and safe procedure when performed by a qualified and experienced healthcare provider. While all surgeries carry some level of risk, complications are rare and usually minor, such as mild bleeding or infection. At Circumcision in London, we take extra care to ensure that the procedure is as safe and comfortable as possible for your child.

Myth 3: Only Infants Can Be Circumcised

Although circumcision is most performed on new born boys, teenagers and even adults can undergo the procedure. Many parents opt to have their child circumcised as a new born for convenience, but it's never too late to consider the benefits of circumcision at any stage of life.

Myth 4: Circumcision is Painful for Infants

Modern circumcision techniques use local anaesthesia to minimise discomfort. Babies typically recover quickly after the procedure, with minimal pain reported afterward. At our clinic, we prioritise patient comfort and use the most advanced methods to ensure a smooth and comfortable experience for your baby with minimal discomfort.

What to Expect During the Procedure

At Circumcision in London, we strive to make the circumcision process as stress-free as possible for both parents and children. Here's a step-by-step overview of what you can expect during your visit:

  • Consultation: Before the procedure, you will have a consultation with our experienced medical team. This is an opportunity to ask questions, discuss any concerns and ensure that you fully understand the procedure.
  • Preparation: On the day of the circumcision, we use a local anaesthetic to ensure that your baby is comfortable and pain-free. Our team of professionals will guide you through the preparation process and explain the steps involved.
  • The Procedure: The actual circumcision typically takes only 10-15 minutes. Our experienced practitioners use techniques to perform the procedure efficiently and safely.
  • Post-Procedure Care: After the circumcision, we will provide you with detailed instructions on how to care for your baby's healing process. Most babies recover within a week and any discomfort they experience can be managed with over-the-counter pain relief.

Conclusion

Circumcision is a personal decision for parents, and it's important to be well-informed about both the benefits and the realities of the procedure. At Circumcision in London, we are here to help guide you through the decision-making process and provide expert care for your child. Whether you're considering circumcision for medical, cultural, or religious reasons, our experienced team is ready to offer the support you need.
